then.text: You met him! I knew it. My granddad said he'd come back when the fen needed him. Mind you, my granddad also said eels could hear the weather.
Ask the verger in the cathedral about the secret path. Then out to the Aldreth causeway in the west, over the bog. Mind the Norman.

else.text: {greeting} Eels. Ely means eel island. In the old days you paid your rent in eels: so many sticks of twenty-five a year. The abbey got four thousand eels a year off one village alone.
My family's caught eels here since forever. And we've a story. Hereward the Wake, the last Englishman who wouldn't kneel to William the Conqueror, hid out on this isle.
There's a knight on the old causeway at night, they say, still guarding it for King William. And a beacon in the reeds no one ever lights.

then.text: Good. Start in the cathedral; the verger knows how Hereward lost the isle. Then the causeway. Then... well. We'll see.

else.text: Smoked, jellied or stewed? Ha! I'm only teasing. The eels are for me.
